Weight Reduction
American Motors Corporation (AMC). AMC stated that no weight reduction in the 1979 Jeep CJ vehicles is possible. They stated that NHTSA was informed that the Jeep CJ vehicles had necessarily increased in weight for 1977, over 1976, but that NHTSA ignored this trend.
International Harvester Corporation (IH). IH stated that it is doubtful that savings in fuel economy could be demonstrated with a reduction of only 50 pounds in vehicle weight. Even though there may be an actual reduction in fuel consumption, IH stated that the EPA test procedure would likely not show a reduction since the inertia weight increments are 500 pounds. This led IH to conclude that considerably more weight reduction on the average would be required to demonstrate an increase in fuel economy using the EPA procedure. IH further stated that if larger weight reductions were required, then the environmental impact associated with higher usage of less energy efficient materials would have to be considered.
